title: Why is my IP blacklisted? | ignixip
description: What a DNS blacklist listing means, how to check Barracuda, SpamCop and UCEPROTECT, and how to ask each list for removal.
summary: Check a listing, ask the right list for removal, and stop the same address being listed again.

cta.heading: See which lists name an IP
cta.text: The blacklist check queries SpamCop, Barracuda and UCEPROTECT, plus AbuseIPDB. It does not query Spamhaus.

faqs.q: Does a clear result on ignixip mean Spamhaus is clear?
faqs.a: No. ignixip does not query Spamhaus. Use the lookup at check.spamhaus.org before you treat an address as unlisted.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay to be removed?
faqs.a: SpamCop and UCEPROTECT Level 1 expire without a fee once the mail stops. Barracuda's removal form is free. UCEPROTECT also sells an optional faster removal.

title: How to fix DMARC failures | ignixip
description: How SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment works, how to read p=none, quarantine and reject, and how to fix the failures reports usually show.
summary: Read a DMARC failure, tell alignment from a bad sender, and move from p=none to reject safely.

cta.heading: Check the mail records for a domain
cta.text: The DMARC check shows the TXT and MX records. The report tool reads an aggregate file in your browser.

faqs.q: SPF passed. Why did DMARC fail?
faqs.a: SPF passed for the envelope domain, and that domain is not aligned with the From address. DMARC needs an aligned SPF pass or an aligned DKIM pass.
Only after reports show that mail you send is already passing. Start at p=none with an rua address, then quarantine, then reject.

title: SPF record explained | ignixip
description: SPF syntax, the ten-lookup limit, the difference between ~all and -all, and why a second SPF record makes receivers return an error.
summary: One TXT record, ten lookups, and a qualifier on all that matches what you actually send.

cta.heading: Look up the TXT records
cta.text: The DNS lookup shows every TXT record on the domain, including the one that starts with v=spf1.

faqs.q: Can I publish two SPF records, one per sender?
faqs.a: No. Two TXT records that start with v=spf1 make the check a permanent error. Put every sender in the same record.
No. It is a soft fail for everyone not listed. It is not an SPF pass, so it does not satisfy DMARC.

title: How to read email headers | ignixip
description: Where to find full headers in Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail, how to read Received and Authentication-Results, and how to spot a forged From.
summary: Copy the raw header, read Received from the bottom, and trust authentication results from your own server.

cta.heading: List the IPs in a header
cta.text: Paste a header block. The analyser finds the IPv4 addresses in your browser so you can open each one.

faqs.q: Which Received line is the sender?
faqs.a: Read from the bottom. Skip your provider's internal hops at the top. The first external address a server you trust recorded is the one to look up.
Yes, by the sender, further down the header. Use the copy added by your own mail server or your provider.

title: How to monitor an IP blacklist | ignixip
h1: How to monitor an IP blacklist
description: Which blacklist and DNS changes are worth an alert, and how to turn on a free daily watch that emails you only when something changes.
summary: A daily check of listings and of SPF, DMARC, DKIM and MX, with email only when the result changes.

cta.heading: Watch an IP or a domain
cta.text: Confirm the mailbox once. ignixip checks daily and writes only when a listing or a mail DNS record changes. Unsubscribe from any message.

faqs.q: Will I get a message every day?
faqs.a: No. The check runs once a day. Mail is sent only after you confirm, and only when a watched listing or DNS record has changed.
No. The blacklist watch uses the lists ignixip queries. Check Spamhaus at check.spamhaus.org when you need that result.
